newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU feed producers urge cut in grain support prices.
newsitem.headline: EU feed producers urge cut in grain support prices.

text.p: European Union grain intervention prices should be cut further so as to make livestock farmers more competitive, the EU feed producers president said.

"Lower grain prices are needed because feed is the biggest item in livestock production costs," Pat Lake, President of the European Compound Feed Manufacturers Association (FEFAC) told Reuters in an interview.
Feedstuffs, notably grain, account for up to 70 percent of livestock production costs.
Lake said the EU must aim to export without subsidies so as to avoid GATT export restrictions.
"That can be achieved by lower feed costs," he said.
The new U.S. Farm Law was designed to encourage beef and dairy exports without subsidies, he said, adding the EU was obliged to open up its market to imports under the world farm trade accord.
Lake noted that the main EU expansion in recent years has been in the export market with little increase in domestic consumption.
"The EU has the capacity to increase exports, especially in the pig and poultry sectors," he said. --Peter Blackburn Brussels Bureau +322 287 6830
